subject: Post-call recap: BrightWorks integration — SDK + function-calling next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Garcia <tom.garcia@brightworks.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightworks.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: BrightWorks integration — SDK + function-calling next steps

Hi Tom / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear context on BrightWorks' roadmap for AI-assisted content enrichment. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Pain points you mentioned:
- Content enrichment latency is killing throughput for nightly batches (current pipeline peaks at ~45k docs/hour).
- Current reranking is expensive and inconsistent — you'd like a faster embedding + rerank flow for top-k retrieval.
- Need deterministic structured outputs for metadata extraction to avoid manual QA in downstream systems.

What we believe is the right fit from today’s discussion:
- SDK integration (server-side) using Redwood's streaming responses for lower tail latency on long prompts.
- Use function-calling to enforce structured outputs (JSON schema for extracted metadata).
- Run an embeddings + reranking pipeline where we embed candidates with our lightweight quantized encoder and do a cosine-similarity pre-filter, then a small-step reranker for top-5.
- Prefix/KV caching for repetitive query patterns to reduce token cost during peak processing.

Technical asks / constraints you shared:
- Must run within BrightWorks' VPC for PII handling during the pilot.
- We need <200ms 99th latency for interactive enrichment endpoints; batch jobs can be relaxed but cost-sensitive.
- Prefer TypeScript SDK + serverless workers for inference requests.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood: send integration guide + sample SDK snippet and a pricing ballpark for a 3-month pilot (attached).
2) BrightWorks: confirm pilot VPC details and a point-of-contact for infra (who we can work with to spin up a private endpoint).
3) Technical spike: Redwood and BrightWorks engineer pair for a 2-3 day POC to validate streaming + function-calling with your sample dataset.

I'll schedule the technical spike once you confirm the infra contact and an availability window.

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (SDK snippets, function-calling example), sample-integration-diagram.png (arch sketch), redwood-pricing-quote.pdf (pilot pricing).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198
From: Tom Garcia <tom.garcia@brightworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightworks.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T14:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightWorks integration — SDK + function-calling next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- VPC / security: we'll engage infra (cc'd: Elena) to provision a customer-controlled subnet and shared peering for the pilot. Expect them to send details by Friday.
- Latency: the 200ms 99th for interactive enrichment is aggressive for our current infra — happy to validate during the spike. We can tolerate 300ms if cost is lower.
- Embeddings/rerank: curious about the quantized encoder you mentioned — what's the typical dimension/size and expected per-embed cost? Also would like to see a small benchmark on precision@5 vs current reranker.

Next: Elena will share the infra contact. Can you send the TypeScript sample and a minimal dataset (1k docs) we can use for the POC? We'll aim to have the infra stubbed out by next week.

Tom
Product Lead, Search
BrightWorks
Tom.Garcia@brightworks.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Garcia <tom.garcia@brightworks.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightworks.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightWorks integration — SDK + function-calling next steps

Perfect — thanks Tom. Quick answers and artifacts attached: 

- Quantized encoder: we typically ship a 768-dimension float16 model quantized to 8-bit with per-channel scales; typical per-embed compute on a T4-equivalent is ~0.6ms and cost ballpark in our pilot quote. I attached a short benchmark (in the integration guide) comparing precision@5 against a baseline reranker on your sample corpus pattern — we see ~8–12% uplift in precision@5 for top-5 in our tests.
- TypeScript sample: included in redwood-integration-guide.pdf (examples > SDK > TypeScript). The snippet shows streaming inference and function-calling with a JSON schema for metadata extraction. Example function-calling stub in the doc: 

  // pseudocode
  const res = await redwood.streamResponse({
    model: 'rw-infer-embed-quant',
    input: prompt,
    functions: [{name: 'extract_metadata', schema: {...}}],
    stream: true
  });

- Minimal dataset: please upload 1k docs to the shared S3 bucket link (I'll send a secure link once Elena confirms VPC and S3 access).

Proposed timeline:
- Fri (10/01): Elena shares infra contact + peering details.
- Week of 10/05: 2–3 day POC (engineer pairing).

I also included a short checklist in the attachment to speed the POC kickoff. Let me know if you want us to handle the initial deployment into your VPC (we can do that under the Private pilot agreement).

Thanks,
Marissa

- 1k sample ingestion script + embedding pipeline
- Streaming tail-latency load harness (10–50 concurrent)
- Precision@5 eval notebook (results in the docs link)

I'll sync with you tomorrow to finalize the POC runbook.
